News.title: Primary teacher caught secretly filming women’s legs after staff found videos posted to school IT system
News.content:
SICK TEACHER Primary teacher caught secretly filming women’s legs after staff found videos posted to school IT system

A SICK primary school teacher was caught filming women’s legs after fellow teachers found the footage on the school’s internal IT system.

Andrew Winkworth, 45, worked at Worlingham Primary School in Beccles, East Suffolk.





He was let go from his job after it was found he had kept several “graphic” videos on his school account.

Winkworth was caught when another teacher stumbled on the footage while searching the school’s internal server for a video of a school performance shot the previous week.

The sick teacher had been off school that day but his account was accessed after he told staff the footage of the performance was on the internal system.

Videos found in Winkworth’s files featured lone women walking through the streets of Norwich.



The footage allegedly focused on their legs and bottoms while the unaware women were “wearing tight clothing.”

After the vile videos were uncovered in March 2022, they were reported to the headteacher.

Winkworth was suspended and subsequently struck off in September the same year.

A misconduct hearing led by the Teaching Regulation Agency (TRA) has now prohibited the teacher, who had worked at the school for 10 years, from teaching indefinitely.



When Winkworth’s school-issued devices were examined, it was found he had linked his own Google account to the tech.

The account featured the same disgusting videos – using metadata it was discovered they had been filmed in Norwich between August 2020 and January 2022.

A witness noted that the footage appeared and then disappeared from Winkworth’s files, suggesting the former teacher had been deleting them.

Nothing inappropriate was found on the school-issued devices themselves, but it is believed they had been used to access the content from Winkworth’s personal Google Drive.

A witness said they were confident Winkworth had filmed the videos himself, as they featured his shoes and included “the legs of an athletic adult male.”



Suffolk Police‘s safeguarding team carried out a probe into the vile teacher’s behaviour but found no evidence of criminality.

The TRA’s report said: “The panel noted that some of the videos showed women who appeared to be accompanied by children, including footage of a woman walking with a young child, and of a young girl walking alongside an adult.

“The panel also noted that in some videos, the individuals filmed appeared to be young females.”

Former teacher Winkworth admitted that he shot the videos, which featured women in tight clothing, for sexual gratification.

Winkworth also stated that he “loved being a teacher” and believed that “he could continue to be a successful and well-regarded member of the profession.”



He had been employed as an educator for some 19 years before being dismissed over the disgusting footage.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Winkworth has been banned from teaching indefinitely and cannot teach at any school, sixth form college, relevant youth accommodation or children’s home in England.

He is only able to apply for the prohibition order to be revoked after April 2030.

News.title: German men must ask army for permission to leave the country for more than three months as it bolsters war efforts
News.content:
WAR FOOTING German men must ask army for permission to leave the country for more than three months as it bolsters war efforts

MEN of fighting age in Germany must obtain permission from the army to leave the country for an extended period under new war preparations.

Effective as of January 1, it applies to anyone planning to stay abroad for over three months – whether for education, employment or travel.





The measure is part of this year’s broad reforms under the Military Service Modernisation Act, but remained unnoticed until now.

“Male persons who have reached the age of 17 must get permission from the responsible career centre of the German armed forces if they wish to leave the Federal Republic of Germany for more than three months,” it says.

Restricting the movements of men of fighting age comes as the country is preparing for a potential Russian attack on NATO within the next two to three years.

In the event of a national crisis such as a war, emergency conscription may be activated.

An army spokesperson said: “The background and guiding principle of this regulation is to ensure a reliable and informative military register for when needed…

“In case of emergency, we need to know who might be staying abroad for an extended period.”

For millions of men in Germany, it remains unclear how the requirement for a travel permit will be implemented in practice – and what happens if they don’t know about it.

According to RND, a large newspaper chain, the Defence Ministry initially declined to explain why the public had not been clearly informed about the new rules.



Germany aims to ramp up the number of soldiers from the current level of 184,000 to between 255,000 and 270,000 soldiers by 2035.

All men born in 2008 or later must now complete a questionnaire about their willingness to serve.

While the survey is mandatory for men, it remains voluntary for women.

If war was to break out, the military would draw on the questionnaires and medical exams for potential recruits.

The country has stopped short of reintroducing mandatory conscription, but hopes boosting numbers will give potential recruits more insight into military life.



The revelation about the new rule comes weeks after Lieutenant General Gerald Funke, the head of the German armed forces support command, said Russian “hybrid warfare” is his biggest concern.

“While in Afghanistan I had a regrettably high but manageable number of wounded, I now have to plan for the possibility of a thousand injured personnel a day,” he told The Times.

“The closer you look at it, the more complex it becomes and the harder it is to imagine.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He added: “What worries me … at the moment is the hybrid side, the covert side: sabotage, sleeper cells, some kind of targeted attacks.

“I can’t rule out the use of long-range missiles. But I think the hybrid threat is very high.”

News.title: My little girl, 12, died saving her sister from drowning in lake – she sacrificed herself & now I want answers
News.content:
NIKI'S BRAVERY My little girl, 12, died saving her sister from drowning in lake – she sacrificed herself & now I want answers

AMANDA Holmes’ phone rang and a frantic voice said: “I can’t find her… she’s gone.”

Nicole Sanders, 12 – known as Niki – had been excited to go swimming at a former quarry during one of the hottest days of the summer – but within minutes tragedy had struck.





The child had quickly got into difficulty at Ducklington Lake, near her home in Witney, Oxfordshire, and disappeared beneath the water, sparking a desperate search.

But by the time emergency crews had pulled her from the water, it was too late.

On July 18 2021, Niki had made the short walk to the lake from her home with her younger sister Tegan, then 10, as well as two other kids and adults known to the family.

Amanda, 44, understands the children were singing and holding hands in a circle in waist deep water when part of the lake bed gave way, plunging them into deeper depths and there was a chaotic panic to get to the shore.

Tegan later told her mum how brave Niki had held her above the surface to ensure she got out.

Mum Amanda told The Sun: “She’s concentrated on keeping Tegan out of the water so she could breathe.

“But after that she disappeared.”



The mum-of-six had warned Niki to stay out of the deeper water, explaining: “She could swim on her back and she could tread water but she wasn’t the strongest swimmer in the world.”

Firefighters waded into the lake after 999 calls were made around 2.35pm and the schoolgirl was pulled out – but by then Amanda estimates she’d been missing for at least 20 minutes.



Resuscitation efforts then lasted an hour, as Niki was blue-lighted but unfortunately nothing could be done.

After the frantic phone call from her friend – one of the adults watching over the children – Amanda said police arrived at the house and took her to John Radcliffe Hospital.

Amanda said: “I’m so protective of the girls. Then one day Niki was just gone.

“She was such a selfless person – she saved her sister’s life.

“She did everything to the best of her ability to make sure Tegan was safe, until it was too much for her.”



Tegan, now 15, is still traumatised from what she saw.

Amanda added: “It’s just so strange to think about it, because she left all happy and 20 minutes later, after they got there, she’d gone.



“I don’t understand how that happened. There are so many questions about that day.”

The family have since moved away from Witney but Amanda has been campaigning for the lake to be closed off and filled in since her daughter’s death.

She said: “There have been a lot of people who have lost their lives in Ducklington Lake, which I didn’t know until I started looking into it.

“There were people in there swimming the day after Niki died, which blows my mind.”

The Sun has approached Witney Town Council for comment.



Swimming and paddling is banned at the lake due to unstable banks and unpredictable water depths – and safety warnings are in place.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

At the time of Niki’s death, the council told the BBC it “completely understands the desire to do something tangible to prevent any further loss of life”.

And it said it was looking to add “additional safety measures” around the lake and was looking to add more signs.

News.title: Shocking moment driver repeatedly rams car into busy pub entrance after ‘row with bouncer’ – as man, 18, arrested
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a driver repeatedly rams a car into a packed pub after a “row with the bouncer”.

The chaotic scenes kicked off in the early hours of this morning outside The Dolphin pub in Kent, as horrified drinkers watched on in disbelief.





In an exclusive video shared with The Sun, a driver repeatedly crashes a black Seat Ibiza into the busy boozer.

Terrified onlookers could be heard screaming and scrambling for safety as the mayhem unfolded.

Witnesses said the carnage erupted moments after the man, believed to be the driver, was thrown out by a doorman following a disturbance inside.



They claimed he had been causing trouble in the pub before being booted out – sparking the shocking attack.

In the footage, staff can be heard shouting: “don’t let anyone out”, as the vehicle lines up outside the entrance.

It waits at the junction opposite the pub for around 10 seconds before suddenly accelerating and smashing into the building.

The person filming backs into the doorway to avoid being hit as the car ploughs forward.



The driver then reverses before accelerating and smashing into the wall a second time.

After the collision, a man opens the passenger door and the driver appears to try and punch the person trying to apprehend him.

People can be heard screaming as Mark Morrison’s hit Return of the Mack blares in the background.

The driver then pulls away from the wrecked entrance, with debris wedged in the front of the vehicle, before speeding off from the scene.

Parts of the Seat were left behind among rubble ripped from the damaged pub building and scattered across the road.



The person filming says in the aftermath of the crash: “Get the police here now.

“He used his car to ram right into the front of building. Unbelievable”.

A girl who had been out with friends that evening said the pub had been “busy” and full of “good vibes” before the horror unfolded.

She said: “Yeah it all all a bit crazy really, when it happened we were all locked in the pub for our safety.

“There was lots of confusion as people didn’t really know what had happened.



“The pub was really busy and up until then the night just pure good vibes.”

Kent Police confirmed an 18-year-old man has since been arrested.

A spokesperson for the force said: “Kent Police was called at 1.56am on Saturday April 4, 2026 to Albion Road, Broadstairs to a report of a car colliding with a building.

“Officers attended the scene alongside other emergency services, where minor injuries were reported.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“An 18-year-old man was arrested in connection with the incident and remains in custody.



“An investigation is underway, anyone with information can contact Kent Police.”

News.title: Wild moment man, 20, wrestles with great white shark on beach after charging into water to free beast from fishing line
News.content:
THIS is the insane moment a brave fisherman wrestles with a great white shark while freeing the beast from a fishing line.

Dramatic footage shows Kevin Phan, 20, tear off his clothes and make a beeline towards the predator, who can be seen thrashing against the waves.





The young Californian had been enjoying an early-morning fishing trip at Hermosa Beach Pier when he spotted the stricken juvenile great white.

As he sprints into the water to make the daring rescue, a large crowd gathers to watch the gripping rescue.

Phan, wearing only boxers and wielding a pair of scissors, enters the water and mounts the shark.

The young fisherman straddles the sharp-toothed beast as it thrashes around in the shallow waters.

He then cuts the shark loose, before bravely guiding it back into the ocean by the tail.

Phan told the Los Angeles Times: “When I saw the great white, my brain just clicked into the action, and I tried to free it as quickly as I could.

“It was a little bit scary because I have never dealt with a white shark before.



“The teeth were a bit intimidating.”

The heroic act, which unfolded shortly after 9am yesterday, was caught on camera by a nearby dogwalker Alexandra Garry.

Garry had spotted two fishermen in a tug-of-war match against the beast, completely oblivious to what was on the end of their line.

She told the LA Times: “I was like, ‘oh that’s so weird, they must have gotten something really big’.

“I thought perhaps it was a big tuna, really anything except for a shark.



“The next thing I knew, one of the fishermen was half naked, stripped down to his underwear, and was in the water trying to get the hook out.”

Phan, a fisherman for the past five years, told the outlet that he hadn’t “intentionally” hooked the animal, as shark fishing is illegal in California.

As beachgoers slowly realised what Phan had caught, amazed onlookers gravitated towards the commotion.

One witness, Stephen Copeland, said: “I saw a bunch of people over there, and I ran down there like there’s something going on. He was in his underwear.”



Bystanders watched in anticipation as Phan cut the beast loose and tossed his scissors into the sand behind him.

In the footage, the shark initially appears disorientated and helplessly rolls back-and-forth with the waves.

Garry said: “It was really sad, because the shark didn’t look like it was moving a bunch.”

But Phan wades back into the water and lifts the beast by the tail, before guiding it into an oncoming wave.

The sea creature manages to regain its balance, earning a ripple of applause from onlookers who had seen the rescue.



“When it swam out, everyone on the pier clapped,” Garry said.

“It was a very much needed moment of humanity.”

In a bizarre turn of events, Phan revealed that it had been the second great white he had accidentally hooked that day.

Marine experts are warning that a busy season full of shark sightings along the Southern California coast are expected this year due to warmer ocean temperatures.



March’s record-breaking heat wave is expected to intensify this year’s El Nino cycle – a natural climate pattern that pushes warm waters towards the Americas every two to seven years.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Chris Lowe, director of the Cal State Long Beach Shark Lab, told the LA Times: “The last time we had a strong El Niño was in 2015 and 2016, and we had a lot of juvenile white sharks hanging around early.

“I’m expecting this year to be a sharky summer.”

News.title: Trump vows to ‘rain all hell’ on Iran if Strait of Hormuz isn’t open within 48 hours & demands regime make a deal
News.content:
DONALD Trump has vowed to rain “all Hell” on Iran if it doesn’t reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours.

The US President demanded that the rogue nation “MAKE A DEAL or OPEN UP THE HORMUZ STRAIT”, telling its leaders ominously that “Time is running out”.





He threatened: “48 hours before all Hell will reign [sic] down on them”.

Trump said earlier this week that “great progress” had been made in crunch peace talks with Iran.

The US president said a deal will “probably” come soon but warned he’ll unleash total “obliteration” if Iran refused to accept his ceasefire deal.



He then threatened to bomb the rogue state “to the Stone Ages” unless the Strait of Hormuz is freed.

It comes as a desperate search is underway to locate a missing American pilot whose F-15 jet was shot down over Iran.

Trump has not officially commented on the desperate search for the serviceman – but the president told a reporter the downed pilot would not affect peace talks, NBC News reported.

Armed Iranians have joined the hunt for the missing airman after they were offered a sick “precious prize” by bloodthirsty broadcasters.



Gun-toting nomads are chasing the American, as the US continues its frantic search effort to bring their fighter home safe.

The US F-15 fighter jet was shot down over Iranian airspace yesterday, with two crew members ejecting over treacherous terrain near the Iraqi border.

It marked the first time a US warplane had been shot down in enemy territory since the six-week war began.

Shocking footage on Iranian social media shows men, who appear to be civilians, armed with rifles patrolling the mountains where the American is thought to be hiding out.

They wave Iranian flags, with one telling the camera: “Don’t worry, we will find them, God willing.”



Upon the discovery of debris from the stricken aircraft, state TV channels urged residents to scour the area for the pilots.

One anchor said: “If you capture the enemy pilot or pilots alive and hand them over to the police, you will receive a precious prize”.



US Central Command meanwhile launched a frantic search – deploying Black Hawks and a low-flying refuelling plane.

One airman was swiftly rescued, but the two helicopters involved were pounded by light weaponry as they made their escape.

They returned safely to Iraqi territory, despite one trailing smoke from the damage.

A sick $60,000 (£45,000) bounty was put on the head of the second pilot, with Iranian TV claiming a propaganda victory for gunning down the US jet.

The Truth Social message threatening to rain “all Hell” on Iran came after two other posts from the US President yesterday.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

In the first, Trump wrote: “We can easily OPEN THE HORMUZ STRAIT, TAKE THE OIL, & MAKE A FORTUNE. IT WOULD BE A “GUSHER” FOR THE WORLD???”.

The second post simply read: “KEEP THE OIL, ANYONE?”

News.title: Sixth person arrested over arson attack on Jewish ambulances – as two men, 20 & 19, and boy, 17, remanded in custody
News.content:
ARSON ARREST Sixth person arrested over arson attack on Jewish ambulances – as two men, 20 & 19, and boy, 17, remanded in custody

COPS have arrested another person in connection with the alleged arson attack on Jewish ambulances as three others are remanded in custody.

Two young men and a boy have been remanded in custody after appearing in court accused of torching four Jewish community ambulances in north-west London.





It comes as the court heard a sixth person was arrested in connection with the alleged arson at court on Saturday morning.

The ambulances from Hatzola, a volunteer-led ambulance service operating in the Golders Green area of north-west London, were set on fire in the early hours of March 23.

The attack caused gas canisters stored in the vehicles to explode, resulting in £1 million worth of damage, Westminster Magistrates Court heard.

British men Hamza Iqbal, 20, and Rehan Khan, 19, from Leyton, east London, and a 17-year-old boy, of dual British-Pakistani nationality, from Walthamstow, are each charged with one count of arson being reckless as to whether life would be endangered.

The accused, who were arrested as part of a Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) investigation, did not enter pleas and were remanded in custody during the hearing, which lasted around 45 minutes on Saturday afternoon.

Prosecutor Emma Harraway told the court: “There is significant evidence that this was a premeditated and targeted attack against the Jewish community.”

Prosecutors do not yet know the motivation for the alleged attack, which “specifically targeted” the ambulances, the court heard.

The case is not being treated as terrorism but CTP said due to “the circumstances of the incident” the investigation is being led by its detectives.



The defendants spoke only to confirm their personal details during the hearing, which took place before a full public gallery of relatives.

As Iqbal, who wore a grey prison-issue tracksuit in the dock, was taken to the cells, a member of the public gallery said: “Take care son, yeah.”

The court heard Khan, who also wore a grey prison-issue tracksuit, is a college student.

Both were remanded into custody, with the 17-year-old, who cannot be named for legal reasons, remanded into youth detention accommodation.

The three defendants are set to appear at the Old Bailey on April 24.

Two other men aged 45 and 47 who were arrested last week, and are also British, were released on bail until late April.

News.title: Texas Killing Fields serial murderer abducted my daughter, 12, as she jogged – major breakthrough ends decades of hell
News.content:
THE mom of a 12-year-old girl murdered in the Texas Killing Fields hopes a long-awaited breakthrough will finally lift the “darkness” that has haunted families for decades.

One of the most chilling episodes in American history received fresh impetus this week after James Elmore Jr., 61, was charged in connection with the 1984 killing of Laura Miller.





He was also accused of tampering with evidence tied to the 1986 murder of Audrey Cook, according to authorities.

Elmore, who lived about eight miles from the stretch of land known as the Killing Fields in League City, Texas where over 30 girls were murdered and dumped from 1970 to the early ’90s, was arrested Tuesday.

He has not been accused of anything else other than the cases involving Miller and Cook.

The cold case saga is a decades-long mystery centered on the area near Interstate 45 between Houston and Galveston in the Lone Star State.

Read more on True Crime NO PROGRESS Brother breaks silence after FBI update on sister's cruise ship disappearance

Cops estimate around 35 women in total were dumped there in the past four decades.

Authorities had recently zeroed in on suspected serial killer Clyde Hedrick, who had been linked to the deaths of Miller and Cook, as well as Heidi Fye-Villareal, who went missing in 1983, and the 1991 disappearance of Donna Prudhomme.

Both Fye-Villareal, 25, and Prudhomme, 34, weren’t identified until 2019.

Prosecutors were preparing to bring charges against him through a grand jury, but Hedrick died by suicide in March before he could face trial.



Officials, however, say the case is far from over, handing families who have desperately been searching for answers fresh hope.

Many involved were unaware how widespread the horror truly was, according to Gay Smither whose daughter Laura was among the victims

The 12-year-old was murdered by another serial killer prowling the area, William Reece, currently on death row in Oklahoma.

“We were completely ignorant of it, and so was everyone else,” Smither, whose daughter had gone out for a jog before being killed and disposed off in a pond, told The U.S. Sun

“Back then, there was no public knowledge of all the unsolved cases in our area. As bad as our case was, Laura was found after 20 days. Those were the worst 20 days of my life, but I have friends whose children have been missing for over 30 years. They are stuck in a spin cycle.”



With the 25-acre site, characterized as a brushy, sprawling wasteland close to highways that allowed perpetrators a quick getaway route, law enforcement agencies lacked coordination at the time, allowing patterns to go unnoticed.

A lack of technology, modern genetic DNA testing, and the absence of social media — which today allows more immediate publicity for such cases— all painfully hindered the investigations.

“It crossed so many jurisdictions, and back then, police departments were very territorial. They didn’t talk to each other at all,” Smither said.

“Laura’s case shone a spotlight on that and forced a change.”

Four victims at the Calder Road burial site — Heide Villareal Fye, Cook, Miller, and Donna Prudhomme — were all identified, as were 12 others aged between 13 and 25 found along the I-45 corridor.



A further nine victims — including 29-year-old Ellen Rae Beason, whose case was re-opened by former Galveston prosecutor Kevin Petroff in 2012 — were found between 1984 and 2016.

When Beason’s body was first discovered in 1984, Hedrick claimed she drowned accidentally while swimming.

He admitted to hiding her body out of fear but denied killing her.

The medical examiner could not determine a cause of death at the time, and Hedrick was convicted only of abuse of a corpse.

When the case was reopened decades later, Beason’s body was exhumed for a second autopsy using modern forensic technology.



This new examination revealed blunt-force trauma to her skull, directly contradicting Hedrick’s accidental drowning story.

However, by the time the case went to trial in 2014, the prosecution lacked sufficient evidence to prove malice aforethought after 30 years. The jury found him guilty of manslaughter.

He was sentenced to 20 years in prison but was released on mandatory supervision in 2021 after serving just eight years.



Hedrick remained on parole until his death last month.

“There are many conspiracy theories surrounding this case, and usually, you roll your eyes at them. But this was truly unusual,” Petroff told The U.S. Sun.

“They had already exhumed Ellen Beeson once, evaluated her, and re-buried her without anything happening. Having to do it a second time was ridiculous. Furthermore, the Medical Examiner (ME) was fighting us and hiding evidence.

“They didn’t fully ‘de-flesh’ the skull. The point of impact—the cause of death—was still covered by skin in the initial photos. When they re-evaluated it and removed the remaining tissue, the trauma became visible.”

Parole laws, Petroff explained, were based on the rules in effect when a crime was committed.



Today, someone convicted of manslaughter with a deadly weapon must serve at least half their sentence, but in the 1980s only a quarter was required.

Older inmates with serious health issues are often released if not deemed a threat — Hedrick, battling throat cancer, qualified for early release.

That sparked local fury, led by Laura Miller’s father Tim who has dedicated his life in the pursuit of justice for his daughter.

According to the indictment released this week, Hedrick allegedly prepared a vial of cocaine for Elmore to give to Cook.

Prosecutors now believe the killings may not have been the work of a lone predator, but a coordinated effort involving multiple individuals familiar with the area.



I’ve learned there is no shortage of these monsters. Mom of murdered 12-year-old Laura Smither

The so-called ‘Killing Fields’ — particularly the Calder Road site — may have served as a disposal ground for a small group.

“It was used as a dumping ground,” Petroff continued. “Littering wasn’t such an issue back then.

“Contractors would drive out there and dump truckloads of debris. Sadly, that culture of dumping trash extended to the bodies of murdered young women.”

Miller, a high school sophomore, was last seen at a pay phone in 1984. Her remains were discovered two years later by boys riding dirt bikes.

Cook, a 30-year-old mechanic, disappeared in 1985; her body was found the following year with a gunshot wound to the back.



The renewed push in the case began in 2024, when the Galveston County District Attorney’s Office re-examined evidence and began focusing more closely on Hedrick.

Advances in DNA technology and new witness information, including Elmore’s recent arrest, have since opened fresh investigative paths.

“There are other active leads in the case; therefore, we’re not going to elaborate on a bunch of detailed questions, because there are some active leads that can still be pursued to bring to justice some people who may have escaped justice thus far,” Galveston County District Attorney Kenneth Cusick said.



Former prosecutor Petroff said breakthroughs in cold cases typically hinge on new science or testimony.

“To win a cold case, you need something new—either scientific evidence or a new witness,” he said. “With current technology like genetic genealogy, new avenues are finally opening up.”

A key figure in that effort has been Miller, Laura’s father and founder of Texas EquuSearch.

Petroff first met Miller when preparing for the Beeson case, and said a prisoner claimed that Hedrick had made admissions about his daughter.

It wasn’t enough to convict him, but Miller fought on with his non-profit search and recovery organization, created in 2000, refusing to stop fighting for justice.



“I can’t imagine what he’s gone through,” said Petroff. “He turned a tragedy into an organization that has benefited thousands of families worldwide. It is truly astonishing.”

In an extraordinary move, he spent years building a relationship with Elmore — meeting him more than 30 times and gathering information that ultimately helped investigators.

The emotional toll was immense

“There were times that I left James Elmore […] and I had to pull over and just sob and cry,” Miller said previously.

He also expressed anger that Hedrick died before his hearing, calling it “inexcusable.”



For families, even major arrests do not bring closure—only something closer to resolution said Smither.

“There is no such thing as ‘closure.’” she stressed. “There is only resolution. This is a life sentence for us.”

She added that the pain never fades, especially for families still searching for answers.

“It is the worst darkness because you are stuck,” Smither said.

There were 6,000 volunteers looking for Laura before she was found on April 20, 1997.



The Texas-based Zimbabwe native started a foundation centered on looking for missing children and helping their distraught families after her daughter’s tragic killing.

The foundation slowed in 2016, the toll becoming too tough to bear.

Smither may close it for good this year, yet over the years became involved in hundreds of cases.

“I had a constant stream of people knocking on my door asking for help,” she said. “It was heartbreaking but at least something positive came from our own situation.”

She thinks the I-45 corridor became a target because of its geography and lack of communication between agencies.



“It’s a major, highly trafficked route,” she said. “Predators knew the police didn’t communicate, so they would move from one place to another to get away with their crimes.”

Over the years, multiple suspects have emerged. Some cases have been solved through DNA, including convictions tied to other victims.

One suspect, Robert Abel, was accused and hounded by Miller (as detailed in a 2022 Netflix documentary) of killing four women found between 1983 and 1991.

He wasn’t charged, and Miller later apologized. Abel, 65, died when his golf cart was struck by a train in 2005. It’s unclear if he took his own life.

Reece was convicted and sentenced to death in 2021 for the 1997 kidnap, sexual assault, and murder of 19-year-old Tiffany Johnston in Oklahoma.



The case remained cold for nearly two decades until 2016, when he confessed during interviews with a Texas Ranger.

DNA evidence from Johnston’s body confirmed his confession.

Following his Oklahoma death sentence, Reece returned to Texas in 2022 to face charges for a string of decades-old cold cases.

He pleaded guilty to the murders of Smither, 17-year-old Jessica Cain, and 20-year-old Kelli Cox, receiving three consecutive life sentences.

Smither fears there are more victims yet to be discovered, telling The US Sun she is concerned about cases in Montgomery County and a Native American woman outside Oklahoma.



Others, however, may never see justice in a courtroom.

Authorities insist the broader investigation is ongoing, and more arrests could follow.

Elmore now faces a manslaughter charge and two felony counts of evidence tampering.

He appeared in court Wednesday wearing a pink prison uniform and was denied bond.

For families like the Smithers, the latest development offers a measure of hope — even if it cannot undo decades of grief.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I’m sure there are more victims than we know about,” Smither said, “and I’ve learned there is no shortage of these monsters. But hopefully, more families will now finally get some kind of resolution.”

News.title: Mum catches woman 'trying to throw her five-year-old out the window'
News.content:
Mum catches woman 'trying to throw her five-year-old out the window'

Things took a terrifying turn when a mother asked her roommate to watch her two children while she ran errands and she came home to find her trying to push her five-year-old out of a window

View Image Vira Zabudko allegedly attempted to to push a five-year-old out of a third-floor window

A mother came home to a nightmare scenario when she caught her roommate allegedly trying to push her child out of a window, before attempting to drown the five-year-old.

‌



The woman, named as Karen Garcia by CBS, had reportedly left her two children - aged five and 11 - with 41-year-old Vira Zabudko while she ran errands. Zabudko is believed to have lived in the same apartment with Garcia and her boys.

‌



According to a criminal complaint obtained by a local ABC affiliate, the mother told police that when she returned to her apartment, Zabudko allegedly would not let her back inside. The mother finally got inside, where she claims she found Zabudko trying to force her five-year-old out of the window through the screen.

‌



Police said a fight then ensued, with Zabudko telling the five-year-old to get in the shower "to wash the sins out because he is dirty". According to the complaint, Zabudko also allegedly tried forcing the mum into the shower area.

Mum-of-one's car message from beyond the grave solves grim murder riddle READ MORE :

Nursery worker who abused 21 babies could be freed after just months behind bars READ MORE :

Thankfully Garcia was able to escape from Zabudko with both her children; police said that when they found the mum and her two sons, they were all soaking wet.

"We are still trying to gather some information, including how long Ms. Zabudko has been in the area, how long they have cohabitated," Fayette County District Attorney Michael Aubele said. "I understand Ms. Zabudko is a Ukrainian national. I am not sure if she has American citizenship or what her status is."

‌



He said he was particularly disturbed by allegations that when Zabudko allegedly pushed the 5-year-old into the bathtub, she said she was trying to wash away his sins.

"I am not really sure what her religious status is, but I don't know of any religion that would reasonably think that throwing a child or drowning a child was going to wash somebody of sins," Aubele said. "There appears to possibly be a mental health element to this, and of course, we will investigate everything, including the possibility of getting a mental health evaluation."

Zabudko has been charged with aggravated assault, two counts of unlawful restraint, two counts of recklessly endangering another person, and simple assault. She was booked into the Fayette County Jail and posted bond. She is due back in court on April 9.

‌



It comes after a teenage babysitter was sentenced to life in prison after killing a nine-year-old boy in his care. Daniel Cameron, who was 15 when the killing occurred , had been paid to babysit Hunter MacIntosh. But according to court documents, he left the house early and was spotted walking through town at 8pm.

At 8.30pm, he sent a Snapchat message to three friends asking "What would you do if I killed someone?". Cameron then followed up with a Facebook message to another friend which said: "What would you think of me if I killed someone?" and then a second message saying, "straightforward answer".

When the victim's mother returned home around 10:30pm she found her child dead with a 25cm knife embedded in his stomach in their home in Otautau, New Zealand.

Article continues below

The post-mortem showed he had received three large knife wounds to his chest and torso and had marks on his neck consistent with asphyxia.

The results from the autopsy suggested the boy had been killed within 90 minutes of being in the babysitter's care. Cameron was quickly arrested at his home after midnight. He pleaded guilty.

News.title: Afghan war hero who fought alongside Brits left fighting for life after station 'assault'
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Afghan war hero who fought alongside Brits left fighting for life after station 'assault'

Hero Noor, 39, who put his life on the line for Britain while working as an Afghan interpreter and fled from the Taliban was left fighting for his life after an alleged attack.

View 7 Images Heroic Noor Aziz Ahmadzai bravely fought alongside Brits in Afghanistan - but has been left with a brain injury following an alleged assault

An Afghan hero who put his life on the line for Britain was left fighting for his life after an alleged attack while working as a security guard in the UK.

‌



Noor Aziz Ahmadzai, 39, had a high-risk role as a translator for British soldiers before being forced to flee Afghanistan dressed as a woman to evade brutal penalties from the Taliban. After a spell of homelessness the dad-of-one tried to rebuild his life in the UK whose interests he had so loyally served, securing a job as a security guard.

‌



But the former Afghan special forces member was allegedly attacked while working this month and left with serious brain injuries from which it may take months to recover - and his doting ex partner has "put her life on hold" to care for him.

‌



Massive data leak saw 100,000 Afghans put in danger as thousands brought to UK READ MORE :

View 7 Images Noor forged a life in the UK after being granted sanctuary following the fall of Kabul

Two teenage girls have been arrested and released on bail following the attack. Mum George Morse has stepped up to care for her ex-partner Noor who now faces a lengthy battle for recovery Noor, with whom George shares a two-and-a-half-year-old son, was rushed to hospital with a serious brain injury on Thursday, March 26.

‌



He is now in a stable but serious condition, and faces a long road to recovery for which George has taken up responsibility. Speaking to the Mirror, family friend Jacqueline Skott, 57, said George, a nurse who helped Noor settle in the UK following his arrival, has travelled to be by his bedside, leaving their son in the care of her parents.

Jacqueline has set up a GoFundMe campaign to ensure George has the help she needs to provide Noor with support, with his road to recovery appearing increasingly complex.

She said dedicated George has "put her life on hold" for her former partner, saying: "She's got a two-year-old son with Noor. She's left her son in Brighton and is renting nearby so she can be at the hospital."

‌



View 7 Images Doting dad Noor was left with a severe brain injury following an incident in Weymouth

George, Jacqueline explained, has taken on Noor's care right before she was due to start a new job at a nursing home, and had put their son into nursery at the time. The incident has thrown her life "into disarray", with George told her former partner's outlook currently remains unclear.

She said: "She was on [the Monday after Noor's hospitalisation] due to start a three-day induction at a nursing home." She added: "Now suddenly, of course, that's not happened because she's been down there. Suddenly her life has been thrown into disarray."

‌



She has been informed that Noor "won't be able to retain any new information or new memories for at least 2 to 3 weeks". Jacqueline added that George has been told by specialists that "it could likely take around 6 months to ascertain the level of any long-term damage".

The time frame for when he may be able to make any significant decisions about his life, including managing his finances, is similarly up in the air, with Jacqueline's fundraiser seeking to provide funds for his specialist support, rehabilitation, and care.

View 7 Images Noor has a long history of working with British forces during his time serving in Afghanistan

‌



Noor is a war hero who has a storied career within Afghanistan's military, having signed up to service aged just 16. Over his decades of service, he worked as a translator for the British military, and later joined the Afghan special forces. The heroic dad eventually became deputy commander of a specialist Afghan counter-terrorism unit that responded to suicide attacks in Kabul, and was among the first at the scene of hundreds of incidents.

Among them, he told Sky News, was the murder of newborns and their mothers during a 2020 maternity clinic massacre, and the Taliban siege of the Intercontinental hotel in 2018.

During the latter operation, his team was joined by British Army personnel, and he said they were together able to bring diplomats to safety, but at the cost of one of his soldier's lives. He said: "We had an order to respond to what was happening... we were joined by the British Army. We saved some diplomats and were able to bring them out.

‌



"I started there at 12 o'clock midnight, and continued till 12 o'clock in the afternoon, until we finished the enemy. I lost one of my soldiers. He lost his life in my hug [in my arms]."

View 7 Images Noor has built a family and career in the UK after being granted sanctuary in 2021

He was given sanctuary in the UK in 2021 following the fall of Kabul alongside more than 1,400 others who had assisted British forces. Afghan interpreters were essential to western fighters in the country between 2006 and 2014, and were hailed as linguistic and cultural "eyes and ears".

‌



At the time Noor spoke of how difficult his life was when the Taliban took back control. "It was a black day for all Afghans who worked with other militaries," he said. Noor was initially arrested at a Taliban checkpoint as a member of Afghan special forces, but was released after a commanding officer claimed - falsely - that he had quit three months before.

He ran four-and-a-half miles home without shoes, his feet covered in blisters. His mother then took him to hide inside a water tank at his sister's house overnight, and he was rescued thanks to the intervention of a colleague from Sandhurst he contacted on Facebook.

"There was an attack on my home, and they shot my family members," Noor said. "My colleague thought I was dead. When I messaged, he told me he was crying that I was alive. He said, 'come to the airport at six in the morning'. Then I put on women's clothes, as the Taliban were stopping cars - but when they saw a woman in the car, they would leave the car alone.

‌



"I used a woman's scarf on my head, and I went to the airport. He came to the gate to get me. My mum just pushed me. She said, 'get out of here', and so I didn't hug her one last time."

View 7 Images Noor sustained significant trauma from his time serving in Afghanistan

The expertise of people like Noor allowed British servicemen and women to work hand-in-hand with Afghan partners and local communities while protecting British troops.

‌



Critical intelligence supplied by interpreters helped identify threats from Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs), saving British lives. The Government later acknowledged a "debt of gratitude" to the thousands of locally employed Afghan citizens who assisted, before it launched specialised resettlement schemes - although some were left pleading the Government for help.

Noor - who was not the only hero left struggling after coming to the UK - and his countrymen who boldly interpreted for western forces, tens of thousands of whom were named in a major data leak from the Ministry of Defence (MoD) in 2023, are still being hunted by the Taliban.

Jacqueline said Noor sustained serious trauma from his time fighting in Afghanistan, making the recovery from his brain injury "a far more complex and precarious road to recovery than it might be for others". Following his resettlement in the UK, he experienced homelessness before starting his family and finding a job as a security guard.

‌



British Transport Police (BTP) confirmed in a statement that officers were called to a railway station at 8.31pm on March 26 following reports that a member of rail staff had been assaulted.

View 7 Images Doting dad Noor has a difficult road to recovery ahead of him

Detective Chief Inspector Paul Atwell said two teenage girls were arrested in connection with the incident, and they have since been released from custody as the investigation continues.

Article continues below

He said: "Our investigation into this extremely concerning incident is ongoing, and two teenage girls, both aged 17, were arrested at the scene in connection. They have been released from custody while our enquiries continue. Our thoughts of course are with the member of staff involved whose family we are supporting.

"We’re keen to hear from anyone who may have witnessed the incident to get in touch with us, either by texting 61016 or calling 0800 40 50 40, quoting reference 741 of 26 March."

People can support the GoFundMe, which has so far raised £5,424 of its £8,000 target from more than 100 donations, by following this link.

News.title: Girl 'too scared to go to school' after horror pupil attack caught on viral video
News.content:
Girl 'too scared to go to school' after horror pupil attack caught on viral video

A teenage girl was left with a broken wrist and whiplash-like injuries after a violent altercation in Bradley Stoke. Her mum says she's now too frightened to return to school

View 2 Images Two girls were attacked in Bradley Stoke, the mother of one said (Image: Submitted)

A shocking video that has gone viral captures a vicious brawl between teenage girls, which one mother claims has left her daughter "scared to go to school".

‌



The violent confrontation erupted in Bradley Stoke on Tuesday, March 31. One of the girls' mums said her daughter was left with a broken wrist and whiplash-like injuries as a result of the altercation.

‌



"She's scared to leave the house, she's scared about her grades because she's too scared to go to school," the mum said. We have chosen not to identify any of the girls involved.

‌



View 2 Images Video footage of the fight shows four girls were involved, with two seemingly trying to leave the area while two other lashed out (Image: Submitted)

Thieves rip safe from wall in Cornwall cider shop raid after horror sledgehammer break-in READ MORE :

The clip, recorded outside a youth club and seen by Bristol Live, shows a girl (Girl A) being punched in the head by another (Girl B) while attempting to defend herself. A third teenager (Girl C), wearing a white t-shirt, retaliates by swinging at the initial aggressor, apparently coming to her friend's aid.

A fourth girl (Girl D), clad in a black hoodie, then wades in, leaving Girl C surrounded by the pair. She tumbles to the ground, dragging Girl B down with her, as Girl D repeatedly strikes her on the head. An adult male is then seen attempting to intervene, while Girl D is heard hurling abuse at Girls A and C.

‌



Girl C is seen walking away from the others, who pursue her around the corner of a building, continuing to shout expletives. The closing moments of the footage are somewhat unclear, but the adult man is seen stepping between the two girls as another scuffle breaks out. The mum said the other group had been hurling food and water at her daughter and her friend.

"One of the bullies punched her in the back of her head," the mum said, explaining that her daughter then rang her and walked away. "That's when one of the girls started attacking [Girl A]. Two jumped on her. [Girl A] got away and now it's two on one."

She said the girls were in tears and hysterical. They headed to a nearby leisure centre while the mum rushed out to reach her daughter.

‌



"I was on the phone with [my daughter] when I got to the youth centre," the mum explained. "I spoke to a random person who said they didn't see anything happening.

"My daughter said 'that's them' and they turned on me. They threatened me, saying they know where I live, they didn't care.

"I was with [my daughter], her friend and a Year 7, trying the keep them safe. I knew I couldn't walk away." The mum added that the police turned up.

‌



Her daughter and daughter's friend experienced lasting consequences from the assault, the mum said. Girl A's teeth were damaged, needing medical treatment, while Girl C has a broken wrist, multiple bruises and muscular injuries similar to whiplash.

"Her GCSEs are soon and she's got to sit in the same room as her attackers," the mum said. "This was the first time they went out together in a while. [Girl C] defended her friend. She will defend a stranger. She wears her heart on her sleeve, she'll do anything for anyone." She added: "I want it to stop. I want children to feel safe."

The footage has been widely circulated on social media, racking up nearly 120,000 views.

Article continues below

The incident comes just a month after a teenage girl was set upon by a gang of boys and girls outside Zara in Cabot Circus. The victim's mum, known only as Stacey, told BristolLive in March how her daughter was followed to the bus stop before being assaulted.

"Luckily, she wasn't badly injured," Stacey said. "She's a bit bruised but there are no injuries. She had concussion and some bruising to her cheeks, a few heel marks on her legs. We're very lucky."

News.title: Thieves rip safe from wall in Cornwall cider shop raid after horror sledgehammer break-in
News.content:
Thieves rip safe from wall in Cornwall cider shop raid after horror sledgehammer break-in

The Bearded Brewery in Cornwall is going cash-free across all its sites after thieves smashed into its St Agnes shop with a sledgehammer and stole a substantial amount from the till and safe

View 3 Images The Bearded Brewery in St Agnes, Cornwall (Image: The Bearded Brewery)

A Cornish brewery has announced it will go cashless after thieves broke into one of its shops and tore a safe clean off the wall.

‌



Police are now probing the break-in at The Bearded Brewery bar and bottle shop in St Agnes, with brewery bosses urging anyone with information to contact officers immediately. The cider shop was targeted at 2am on Wednesday, April 1, with raiders making off with a "substantial" amount of cash from both the till and safe.

‌



The incident has prompted the business to stop accepting cash across all its sites in Newquay, Mawgan Porth, St Agnes and its headquarters in St Mawgan.

‌



View 3 Images Robbie Langouroux-Fay and 'Sparky' (left) at the Bearded Brewery in St Mawgan with their cider 'Unshaven Maiden' which the industry body The Portman Group is trying to ban as being too sexual (Image: Bearded Brewery)

Storm Dave forecast to hit UK with 90mph horror winds in just HOURS - full list of 25 areas at risk READ MORE :

Kris Gillespie, site manager at the St Mawgan brewery, told CornwallLive: "People broke in and took cash from the till and the safe. A substantial amount for us. The lock was punched out with a sledgehammer. They ripped the safe off the wall.

‌



"We are a micro brewery with small premises and this will have a knock on effect for us. So unfortunately we will go cash free from now on."

Mr Gillespie confirmed police had been notified but believed no arrests had been made at this stage. He said: "We are appealing for anyone in St Agnes that saw anything to contact the police."

View 3 Images The lock that was damaged by a sledgehammer at at break-in at The Bearded Brewery in St Agnes (Image: The Bearded Brewery)

Article continues below

The Bearded Brewery was established roughly 10 years ago by Robbie Langouroux-Fay and Mark "Sparky" Long, after the pair originally brewed cider for a wedding. The venture was subsequently established with a brewery close to the airport at St Mawgan, which has since expanded to encompass a five-acre events field along with bar and bottle shops in Newquay, St Agnes and Mawgan Porth.

The company also distributes its craft cider to retailers throughout the UK, with varieties including Carnanton Stag, Cherried Treasure, Just Peachy, Moustache Mango and Tank Slapper.

In addition, it produces cherry brandy, spiced rum and sloe gin, while also offering merchandise such as hoodies, t-shirts, pint glasses and tote bags.

News.title: New arrest over Golders Green arson attack after police 'recognise man in court'
News.content:
New arrest over Golders Green arson attack after police 'recognise man in court'

Three suspects appeared in Westminster Magistrates' Court today charged in connection with the offences, while another arrest was made at the court itself this morning

Ambulances left destroyed after arson attack in Golders Green

Another arrest has been made today in connection with the police investigation into an arson attack on volunteer-led ambulances run by the Jewish community in Golders Green.

Three suspects appeared in Westminster Magistrates' Court today charged in connection with the offences, meanwhile cops made a further arrest at the court building after spotting a 19-year-old man at the court who cops “recognised as being involved”, police said.

The arrest was announced by prosecutor Emma Harraway during a hearing at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Saturday. The arrest was made at the court on Saturday morning, Ms Harraway said.

Scotland Yard said in a statement: “While attending the hearing of three other suspects, officers recognised the man as being involved in the arson attack. He was arrested for arson with intent to endanger life and taken into custody.”

View 2 Images Court artist sketch by Elizabeth Cook of Hamza Iqbal (left), 20, Rehan Khan (right), 19 at Westminster Magistrates' Court (Image: PA)

The teen was arrested for arson with intent to endanger life and taken into custody, making him the sixth person to be arrested in connection with the incident. Three other people have been charged in connection with the arson attack, MyLondon reports.

Hamza Iqbal, 20, and Rehan Khan, 19, both British nationals from Leyton, and a 17-year-old boy of dual British and Pakistani nationality from Walthamstow, were charged on Friday, April 3, with arson being reckless as to whether life would be endangered.

All three appeared at Westminster Magistrates’ Court today (Saturday, April 4) where they were remanded in custody to appear at the Old Bailey on Friday, April 24.

View 2 Images Burnt out ambulances run by a Jewish organisation after they were set on fire in Golders Green (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

They were arrested on Wednesday, April 1, at different locations in east London and officers from Counter Terrorism Policing London carried out searches at each of their addresses.

The arrests and charges are linked to the ongoing investigation into an arson attack at approximately 1.35am on Monday, March 23. Four ambulances from Hatzola, a volunteer-led ambulance service operating in the Golders Green area of north London, were set on fire during the incident.

Two other men aged 45 and 47 were arrested on Wednesday, March 25, have both been released on bail until later this month, pending further enquiries.

News.title: Treasury urged to scrap VAT for youth clubs and community centres
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Treasury urged to scrap VAT for youth clubs and community centres

Labour's sister party pointed out museums and galleries are eligible for a refund on VAT to reflect their public value, while vital community buildings were forced to shell out

View 3 Images Joe Fortune has written to the the Treasury calling for more support

Community centres and youth clubs across Britain are struggling to pay for repairs and upgrades due to excessive VAT costs, the Co-operative Party has claimed.

‌



Labour's sister party pointed out museums and galleries that offered free access are eligible for a refund on VAT to reflect their public value, while vital community buildings were forced to shell out.

‌



This has left buildings struggling to afford vital works, or facing more expensive prices to do so.

‌



Angela Rayner calls for alternative to renting and owning in major housing intervention READ MORE :

View 3 Images Burntwood Memorial Hall needs a new boiler

View 3 Images Baldock Community centre wants to invest in a cooling system

‌



General Secretary of the Co-operative Party Joe Fortune has now written to the Treasury, urging them to extend the VAT Refund Scheme. In the letter, he said: “Community centres often operate on limited budgets, relying on volunteers to keep their doors open. The inability to recover VAT on necessary repairs places an additional financial burden on these organisations, often limiting their capacity to remain open, safe, and accessible to the public.

“The government has made important progress in strengthening community pride, not least through the Pride in Place programme and the measures in the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Bill boosting community ownership. But community buildings suffered under years of austerity as well as the impacts of the pandemic, and for many repairs have become unaffordable, risking their closure.”

Paul Taylor, Trustee and Chair at Burntwood Memorial Community Association, told this newspaper his community was struggling to afford a new boiler due to VAT. He said: “At Burntwood Memorial Hall, we need to replace our central heating boilers for about £10,000, including £1,667 VAT we cannot reclaim. For a volunteer-run charity, this is a big extra cost—money that could help maintain the building, improve facilities, and keep charges affordable for local groups.”

Article continues below

Alistair Willoughby, Trustee of the Baldock Community Hub, shared his own concerns about repairs. He said: “Buildings like this are vital for bringing our communities together. Across the country, village halls, town halls, and community‑run spaces host everything from warm hubs to youth groups, coffee mornings to public meetings. Support from government with these essential works would make a real difference and help us keep serving local people for years to come.”

The Treasury was approached for comment.

News.title: Storm Dave tracker: UK braces for 90mph severe wind warning - weather maps where you are
News.content:
Storm Dave tracker: UK braces for 90mph severe wind warning - weather maps where you are

Storm Dave is forecast to arrive in the UK tonight, with 12 inches of snow and severe wind warnings across Scotland, England, Wales, and Northern Ireland - and you can follow the storm path with the Mirror's tracker

View 4 Images Storm Dave tracker as the UK braces for mega 90mph winds and huge snowfall (Image: Windy.com)

The UK is bracing for the arrival of Storm Dave tonight, which was forecast to bring 90mph wind gusts and up to 12 inches of snow.

‌



The low-pressure system was named by the Met Office earlier this week, and is the fourth named storm of the season. It was expected to reach the UK at about 5pm today, with the most severe weather into the night, from 7pm.

‌



An area of low pressure was expected to rapidly deepen, bringing very strong winds to northern regions. Heavy rain and blizzard conditions were also forecast for the Scottish Highlands. You can follow Storm Dave using the Mirror's storm tracker below.

‌



The Met Office issued a rare Amber warning for wind, ahead of the impending arrival of Storm Dave. The fresh alert was released earlier this afternoon, just hours before Storm Dave was forecast to batter multiple parts of the country.

Storm Dave WATCH LIVE as webcams from around UK show horror 90mph winds smash Britain READ MORE :

Storm Dave forecast to hit UK with 90mph horror winds in just HOURS - full list of 25 areas at risk READ MORE :

The national weather forecaster said Storm Dave was expected to "bring a spell of disruptive and potentially damaging winds" on Saturday night and into the morning of Easter Sunday across the regions covered by the amber alert.

‌



The forecaster said Brits residing in the 25 locations - active from 7pm today until 3am on Sunday - should expect extended journey times or even cancellations of air, ferry and rail services. The Met Office also warned that "flying debris is likely and could lead to injuries or danger to life". Weather experts previously warned that Storm Dave could bring up to 90mph winds in the most northern regions.

View 4 Images (Image: MET OFFICE)

But, the storm would likely only be felt in the north of the UK, according to weather expert Jim Dale. At its very peak, some regions could see wind gusts of up to 90mph, he said.

‌



"It's a northern event, it's not a southern event at all," he told the Mirror. "The real brunt of it will be in the West and North Scotland.

"The low pressure area, Storm Dave, will come over the western side of Ireland, over the top of Northern Ireland, into western Scotland and out through the doors of northeast Scotland towards the Shetlands, all by the time he gets to Sunday morning.

View 4 Images (Image: WXCHARTS)

‌



"It'll bring, at a peak anyway, 80 to 90mph gusts to North and West Scotland, and 60 to 70mph across most of Scotland. Coming south, into Northern Ireland and Northern England, I would expect 50 to 55mph gusts at times. Then as you go further south, only about 40mph in the Midlands.

"Now it isn't just the wind, because with that will come driving rain and blizzard conditions for the higher hills and mountains of Scotland.

"The reason I mention this more than anything is because people are out and about. They will be climbing places like Glencoe and Ben Nevis. Setting off early on Saturday morning, on these hills and mountains, or taking a boat out into the sea, they're gonna get caught out. It's as simple as that."

‌



View 4 Images (Image: Ventusky)

Travel was expected to be disrupted for one of the busiest weekends of the year, owing to the extremely strong winds and snowy conditions. The RAC urged drivers to take extra care on motorways, as well as on higher ground.

RAC spokesperson Rod Dennis said: “The arrival of Storm Dave is set to make driving conditions across the north and west of the UK this Easter particularly challenging. While we expect leisure traffic volumes to be slightly lower on Saturday and Sunday compared with the rest of the bank holiday, there will still be millions of people on the roads visiting friends and family.

Article continues below

"Drivers shouldn’t underestimate the impact of the very strong winds that are forecast. We recommend taking extra care on exposed, higher routes and being especially cautious when overtaking high‑sided vehicles, as the buffeting effect can catch some people out. Slowing down and keeping a firm grip on the steering wheel are both vital in these conditions.”

News.title: Stephen Lawrence's dad braces for fresh battle over son's racist murder
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Stephen Lawrence's dad braces for fresh battle over son's racist murder

Gary Dobson has been refused a move to an open prison but is expected to make a bid for freedom this year after fellow convicted killer David Norris was exposed over his 'cynical' attempt

View 9 Images Stephen Lawrence was stabbed to death in April 1993 (Image: PA)

Stephen Lawrence's father has said he expects another of his son's killers to apply for parole soon as he prepares to oppose the bid.

‌



Gary Dobson, 50, is coming to the end of his minimum term after being jailed in 2012 for the racist murder of Stephen, 18, in South-East London in 1993. Fellow convicted killer David Norris, 49, was denied his "cynical" bid for freedom last year over concerns he may still pose a danger to the public.

‌



Dobson was jailed in 2012 for a minimum of 15 years and two months for the murder and his minimum term expires early next year. Stephen's father, Neville Lawrence, 84, said: "We are waiting to hear because I'm sure he's going to try to get parole as well. But no matter what they try to do there's always ways to make it harder."

‌



View 9 Images Neville Lawrence continues to fight for his son (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Stephen Lawrence racist killer and Manchester bomb plotter clash behind bars READ MORE :

It is understood Dobson, who was in category C HMP Warren Hill in Suffolk, had a bid to be moved to open prison rejected two years ago. The fact he qualified for consideration for a pre-tariff review, which is not mandatory, indicates he is regarded as having made progress during his sentence.

View 9 Images Gary Dobson (left) and David Norris are coming to the end of their sentences (Image: CROWN PROSECUTION SERVICE/AFP vi)

‌



Dobson told police that on the night of the murder he visited Neil and Jamie Acourt to borrow a Bob Marley CD and smoke a joint. He claimed that during the 15 minutes he was there a pal, Matthew White, called to tell them of the murder about an hour after it happened.

When police made house-to-house inquiries Dobson said he did not think it was necessary to tell them he had gone out after the time of the murder, around 10.35pm. He also denied knowing Norris. But he was convicted after the jury heard a stain on his jacket was from Stephen's fresh blood.

View 9 Images Matthew White was said to have told Dobson about the murder soon afterwards (Image: BBC)

‌



Jailing Dobson and Norris at the Old Bailey, Mr Justice Treacy admitted the sentences could be seen as soft but insisted his hands were tied. He told them: "In modern times an adult committing this crime would be facing a life sentence with a starting point for a minimum term of 30 years."

Mr Lawrence said that Norris should also remain in jail after it emerged during his parole hearing in October that he showed signs of continuing to hold racist views. Norris threw excrement at Muslim prisoners, used the N-word and reportedly told his daughter he did not want Black grandchildren.

View 9 Images Neville Lawrence will fight to stop his son's killers being released (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

‌



Mr Lawrence said: "You're then talking about not wanting any Black people in your family and you're going to tell me you've changed? I think he's better off where he is." At the public hearing, Norris spoke for the first time about his role in the knife murder, having previously denied being at the scene.

Stephen was killed during an attack by five or six youths but Norris refused to name the others involved, saying that he feared for his family's safety. Mr Lawrence watched his son's killer give evidence via a live video link in the British Embassy in Jamaica, where he lives for most of the year.

View 9 Images Norris appears via video-link during his parole hearing (Image: Julia Quenzler / SWNS)

‌



He said: "This man has always denied being there. In the first place he said he wasn't there, his mother and himself committed perjury in the trial. He said that he didn't leave the house that night and the mother said he didn't leave. I was just watching to see if he was going to start naming these people, because these are the guys who are walking up and down as free as a bird.

"He said his life would be in danger if he names the rest of the people. This man now has admitted being there. If you can't name these people then what kind of a person are you?" Mr Lawrence also spoke of his shock when he learned he was spied on by undercover police officers.

An inquiry heard in November that officers gathered information about the family’s justice campaign, including in 1998 that Mr Lawrence and his then-wife Baroness Doreen Lawrence were splitting up.

‌



View 9 Images Baroness Doreen Lawrence has fought for justice for her son (Image: PA)

He said: "When I found out I asked my solicitor, was it me who killed my son? Why are you sending people after me to watch to see what I am doing? If you had done your job that you're supposed to do to arrest these people and send them to prison you wouldn't have to be sending someone to watch me.

"I didn't do anything that was violent, I didn't do anything against the law. All I did was to try and publicise what had happened to my son with the interest that by publicising it someone might come along and say who did it. We've been through hell and back and one of the things that I said to myself is "I'm not going to give up."

‌



Outrage over the claims that Stephen’s family had been spied on was one of the key catalysts for the mammoth Undercover Policing Inquiry, which began in 2015. Mr Lawrence told the Daily Mirror on Monday of his anger at plans to drop a key recommendation of the landmark report into his son's racist murder.

View 9 Images Jamie Acourt was later jailed for drug dealing (Image: PA)

He said he had not been consulted over the decision by police chiefs to call for the scrapping of non-crime hate incidents. NCHIs are defined as being motivated by hostility or prejudice towards people with certain characteristics, such as race or gender, but do not meet the bar for a criminal offence.

‌



Sir William Macpherson's 1999 report into Stephen's murder recommended that the term "racist incident" should explicitly include both crimes and non-crimes.

View 9 Images Duwayne Brooks was with his friend when he was murdered

Stephen was stabbed to death as he waited for a bus with pal Duwayne Brooks, now 51. Brothers Neil and Jamie Acourt were accused of being in the gang and have served time for drug dealing. Another, Luke Knight, remained free. All deny involvement.

Article continues below

The sixth suspect was Matthew White, who died at 50 in 2021. He was named for the first time two years later by the BBC who exposed a series of police failings relating to him.

The CPS ruled in 2024 that four officers involved in the botched Met probe would not face charges.

News.content:
